transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-19 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Telltide CISO), Ravi Kapoor (CTO), Liam O'Neill (Platform)
notes: Shared security links: SOC2 report (link: https://redwood.example.com/soc2), private deployment whitepaper (link: https://redwood.example.com/private-deploy), KMS/HSM integration guide (link: https://redwood.example.com/kms)
body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — we have Maya and Diego from Redwood, and Asha, Ravi and Liam from Telltide?
[00:10] Asha: Yep that's us. We'll be mainly focused on security and compliance requirements today.
[00:18] Diego: Great, overview goal is to understand your posture and see where Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private make sense. I'll call out tradeoffs — latency, encryption, auditability.
[00:32] Ravi: Top line — we run inference for patient triage workflows, PII in prompts, so encryption in transit and at rest is mandatory, plus we need strong audit logs and RBAC.
[00:42] Liam: We also need SSO integration with Okta and strict retention controls, ideally 90 days for raw request logs, 365 days for audit trail metadata.
[00:55] Diego: Understood. Quick note: Redwood Hosted is the fastest to spin up, supports token-level logs and per-route tracing but by default retention is shorter and logs are multi-tenant — you can enable longer retention for audit but that usually comes with contract terms.
[01:12] Maya: For Dedicated, you get reserved GPU capacity and tenant isolation — we can offer longer log retention and private VPC peering. For Private (on-prem/VPC), you get full control — customers manage KMS and HSM if they want.
[01:30] Asha: Can you expand on the KMS options? We require HSM-backed key management for encryption at rest.
[01:38] Diego: Yes. We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) with the option to attach HSM-backed keys. For private customers we can integrate with on-prem HSMs via KMIP or a dedicated HSM gateway. Note: that path is part of our Private deployment package.
[01:56] Ravi: How about audit logs? We need immutable logs, tamper evidence and the ability to pull them into our SIEM.
[02:04] Maya: We have an audit logging pipeline — logs can be routed to your S3 or a syslog endpoint, and we provide an append-only audit trail and signed manifests for retention snapshots. We also offer real-time log streaming for SIEM ingestion.
[02:22] Liam: Is the audit trail per-request or per-session? We need per-request metadata including request id, user id, model, tokens in/out, route used.
[02:31] Diego: We emit request-level metadata, including request ID, model variant, route and token counts. Note: by default we redact prompt bodies for hosted customers unless you opt in to full-text logging — that's a compliance control.
[02:46] Asha: Redaction policy — does Redwood do deterministic redaction or do we need to implement client-side masking?
[02:54] Diego: We recommend client-side masking for PII, but for auditability we can also store redaction markers server-side. There is a config flag in Dedicated/Private to change redaction level.
[03:06] Maya: On certifications: we are SOC 2 Type II and maintain ISO27001 summary — I'll share both docs. For private deployments we provide a checklist to help you reach your internal audit bar.
[03:18] Ravi: Great. About RBAC and SSO — we use Okta with SAML 2.0; need fine-grained roles for engineers vs auditors vs ops.
[03:28] Maya: Redwood Console supports RBAC with role templates (admin, dev, auditor) and you can map SAML groups to roles. For Private we can extend with your internal LDAP.
[03:40] Liam: Any limitations on session length or token expiration for SSO sessions? We need sessions to expire at 1 hour for engineers, longer for service accounts.
[03:48] Diego: Session TTLs are configurable via the console for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private you control session policies. We also support service tokens with fine-grained scopes and expiration.
[04:03] Asha: About data residency — we have EU patients and need data not to leave EU region. Does Redwood enforce region pinning?
[04:11] Maya: Yes we offer region pinning for Hosted with EU-only processing. Dedicated can be placed in a specific region or on Dedicated hardware in your cloud project. Private gives the most control.
[04:23] Ravi: There's often talk about "sidecar" logging or network egress — we need to ensure no telemetry leaks to third-party analytics.
[04:31] Diego: For sensitive workloads we can disable analytics telemetry and metrics ingestion; Dedicated and Private offer options to opt out entirely. Hosted has limited telemetry disabled under enterprise contracts.
[04:45] Liam: Curious about model provenance and model catalog security — how do we know model artifacts haven't been tampered with?
[04:52] Diego: We sign model artifacts and keep a model registry with immutable hashes. For Dedicated/Private we can set up your own model signing key and verify at deployment time.
[05:03] Asha: What's your incident response posture? SLA for incident notifications and forensic logs?
[05:10] Maya: Enterprise SLAs include defined MTTR windows, notification timelines, and a runbook for Major incidents. We provide forensic copies of logs for audits; for Private we give full access.
[05:22] Ravi: About retention windows — you said logs can be sent to our S3. Is it possible to enforce retention deletion policy programmatically? We need automatic purging after 90 days for raw prompts.
[05:31] Diego: Yes, you can configure retention policies on the storage endpoint and we can also enforce in-platform retention rules. For Hosted, longer retention requires an add-on and contractual terms.
[05:44] Maya: There was a question earlier about latency vs encrypted traffic — if you enable end-to-end client-side encryption it adds CPU cost. For inference latency sensitive workloads, we typically recommend server-side encryption with customer-managed KMS because the HSM handshake is outside the hot path.
[06:00] Liam: You mentioned KV cache before — for patient triage we may pin long contexts. How is KV cache persisted and who can access it?
[06:09] Diego: The KV cache is ephemeral in memory for active sessions; we persist cache snapshots for warm restarts to encrypted storage. Access is restricted by RBAC and logged in audit trails.
[06:21] Asha: Do you perform any PII scanning or redaction automatically?
[06:26] Diego: We have optional PII detection tools as part of Redwood Optimize — it's configurable and can auto-mask PII before it's stored. But for compliance we recommend client-side masking as primary.
[06:40] Ravi: For Private deployment, network topology — do you support air-gapped installs? Our security team sometimes requires an offline deployment.
[06:48] Maya: We do support air-gapped on-prem installs through our Private package. That includes OVA images or container bundles and a secure operator-run onboarding. It does add to deployment time and requires an SOW.
[06:59] Liam: How do you handle software updates in air-gapped environments?
[07:04] Diego: We provide signed update bundles and a documented process. You perform the update and we provide verification scripts.
[07:12] Asha: Any third-party pen test reports or vulnerability disclosure program details?
[07:18] Maya: We run annual pen tests and maintain a vulnerability disclosure program. We'll share redacted summaries and the process for submitting issues.
[07:29] Ravi: Let's talk about keystore lifecycle — key rotation cadence and compromise procedures.
[07:35] Diego: We recommend a 90-day rotation for ephemeral keys and annual rotations for long-term keys. For customer-managed KMS you control rotation, and Redwood supports automatic rekeying of session keys without downtime.
[07:49] Liam: If we host Dedicated in our VPC, can we bring our own GPUs and still have Redwood manage the serving layer?
[07:58] Maya: There's a Hybrid Dedicated offering where you provide infrastructure and Redwood runs the serving runtime. It requires a network setup and constrained maintenance windows.
[08:09] Asha: Any compliance differences between SOC2 and ISO that we should be aware of for your hosted offerings?
[08:16] Diego: SOC2 focuses on controls mapping to Trust Services Criteria; ISO27001 is more about the ISMS. For customers, SOC2 Type II reports give operational control evidence. ISO certs show broader program maturity. We provide both summaries.
[08:32] Maya: We also support contractual security addenda for data handling specifics and DPA clauses.
[08:38] Liam: About token-level cost breakdowns — are usage logs granular enough to do chargebacks?
[08:44] Diego: Yes, token-level usage logs and per-route cost metrics are exposed in the Console and via the billing API. You can export them to your internal finance pipeline.
[08:56] Asha: Can we do a short technical benchmark — 2 hours — to see tail latency with our real prompts?
[09:02] Maya: Absolutely. Diego can run a bench with Dedicated or hosted mirrored traffic; we'll need a dataset and expected QPS.
[09:11] Diego: For an apples-to-apples, Dedicated will generally have more consistent tail latency given reserved GPU pools. Hosted might have slightly higher p99s but lower ops overhead.
[09:24] Ravi: What about runtime determinism and reproducibility for model outputs? For auditability, we need to reproduce outputs during investigations.
[09:33] Diego: We store model versions and RNG seeds, and for deterministic models we can pin seed and config. For non-deterministic models we capture model version, temperature, and full request metadata to help reproduce.
[09:50] Liam: Will the logs include user identifiers but not the PII content if redaction is enabled?
[09:56] Diego: Correct. You get user id, request id, route and metadata; prompt content is either redacted or omitted depending on config.
[10:07] Asha: For audits we sometimes need a snapshot of raw requests for a short window — can Redwood accommodate time-boxed access?
[10:15] Maya: Yes, with proper approvals and an NDA we can provide time-boxed forensic snapshots. This is typically part of enterprise engagement.
[10:27] Ravi: Ok, from a timeline perspective we plan to decide on a path by end of month. If we choose Dedicated, what's the onboarding timeline?
[10:35] Maya: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 4–6 weeks for standard stacks and 8–12 weeks for hybrid or on-prem setups. Private air-gapped is usually a longer engagement because of SOW and ops.
[10:47] Liam: Who will be our SE contact for the technical deep dive?
[10:51] Maya: Diego will lead the deep dive and will need network diagrams and Okta metadata.
[10:56] Diego: I'll also prepare a checklist for required firewall rules, peering, and any port opens.
[11:05] Asha: Slight transcription note — earlier we said "KV cache" and sometimes the notes show "k v cache", just to be clear it's the model KV cache.
[11:12] Diego: Yes. KV cache = key-value cache in the transformer runtime, ephemeral per session unless snapshot persisted.
[11:20] Ravi: Any gotchas around encryption in transit for internal east-west traffic in Dedicated?
[11:27] Diego: For Dedicated we encrypt east-west traffic by default inside the cluster; for on-prem/private we'll align with your network encryption policies.
[11:35] Liam: On alerts and monitoring — we need SLOs and alert routes into PagerDuty.
[11:41] Maya: Console supports alerting hooks to PagerDuty, Slack, and webhooks. SLO configs are per-route.
[11:51] Asha: We need to understand cost implications: long retention + KMS + dedicated GPUs — can you show cost delta?
[11:58] Maya: We'll include a sample cost delta in the pricing doc; high level — retention and dedicated capacity are the biggest drivers. Diego: quantization and batching options in Redwood Optimize can lower per-token cost.
[12:12] Ravi: Are there any compliance blockers for EU patient data using Hosted with EU region pinning?
[12:20] Diego: As long as data processing is pinned to EU and you control keys in EU KMS, Hosted can be compliant for many scenarios. For maximum assurance use Dedicated or Private.
[12:34] Liam: How do we validate the signed model artifacts on our side?
[12:40] Diego: We provide a signature and public key; verification scripts are open-source in our client repo.
[12:48] Asha: Let's recap — Maya to share SOC2/ISO docs and pricing, Diego to prepare technical SOW/pricing and checklist, Ravi/Liam to provide Okta metadata and retention policy; schedule deep dive next week.
[12:58] Maya: Correct. Anything else?
[13:02] Ravi: Quick question — do you have examples of customers in healthcare who've done a Private air-gapped install?
[13:09] Maya: We have references, will share an anonymized case study and contact under NDA.
[13:16] Liam: Thanks folks, that covers our major concerns.
[13:20] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite for the SE deep dive.
[13:26] Asha: Thanks all.
[13:30] End of call.
